title: Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks
notes: Analytic large-N Lyapunov distribution for autonomous random asymmetric nonlinear RNNs; finite-N response identity and cavity/self-consistent step. Not a trained-language-model or reasoning-performance result. Reference code: https://github.com/davidclark1/rnn-lyapunov. Mathematical limit-exchange assumptions require independent scrutiny.

title: Lyapunov spectra of chaotic recurrent neural networks
notes: Full-spectrum numerical/convergence controls; attractor dimension, external time-varying drive, and some trained RNN dynamics. Direct empirical comparator to Clark; not an LLM reasoning result.

title: On Lyapunov Exponents for RNNs: Understanding Information Propagation Using Dynamical Systems Tools
venue: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics 8:818799
notes: Algorithmic spectrum estimation for non-autonomous, data-driven RNN/LSTM trajectories; demonstrates training-stability relationships on character modeling and motion capture. Useful QR/JVP reference; no universal quality predictor established.

title: Lyapunov-guided representation of recurrent neural network performance
notes: AeLLE autoencoder of Lyapunov spectra correlates with RNN accuracy and early training trajectories on tested tasks; a useful demanding predictive-baseline candidate, not evidence of zero-cost online recurrence-depth selection. Supplementary-file correction doi:10.1007/s00521-024-10366-0. Code: https://github.com/shlizee/LyapunovAutoEncode.

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
venue: ICML 2026, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 306:144670–144682
notes: STARS regularizes Jacobian spectral radius during training with sampled loop counts to avoid recurrence-depth quality collapse. Training-stage intervention distinct from offline spectral diagnosis, proof of general reasoning gains, or inference-only stabilization. Authors' code: https://github.com/njuyxw/STARS.

title: Fractal basins trap latent reasoning
notes: Reports transient-chaos/fractal-basin signatures associated with challenging reasoning trajectories. Observable reasoning traces, model state, and asymptotic internal Jacobian spectra must be kept distinct; causal/necessary-hardness interpretations not imported as validated fact.

title: Linking Connectivity, Dynamics, and Computations in Low-Rank Recurrent Neural Networks
notes: Random-plus-low-rank recurrent connectivity yields analytically tractable low-dimensional task-related dynamics, with clear limits on applying results to trained Transformers. Reproduction examples: https://github.com/fmastrogiuseppe/LowRank.

title: Engineering recurrent neural networks from task-relevant manifolds and dynamics
notes: Constructs RNNs to realize known task-related manifold dynamics and uses Jacobian constraints; well-specified positive synthetic control for task-vs-nuisance decomposition, not an observation that arbitrary trained models have this structure. Code: https://github.com/elipollock/EMPJ.

title: Opening the Black Box: Low-Dimensional Dynamics in High-Dimensional Recurrent Neural Networks
notes: Established fixed-point and slow-point search plus local linearization in trained RNNs. Slow points, asymptotic Lyapunov spectra and useful task information are distinct.

title: Structure, disorder, and dynamics in task-trained recurrent neural circuits
notes: Separate Clark-led trained-RNN analysis: learned structured connectivity and task-relevant low-dimensional dynamics can coexist with random heterogeneity in studied RNNs. Empirical bridge to random-network reference, not a general Transformer theorem. Code: https://github.com/davidclark1/RNN-Learning-Theory.

title: Dynamical Isometry and a Mean Field Theory of RNNs: Gating Enables Signal Propagation in Recurrent Neural Networks
venue: ICML 2018, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 80:873–882
notes: Random-initialization RNN Jacobian singular-value propagation, gated minimalRNN, signal timescales and trainability. Not an asymptotic trajectory Lyapunov-spectrum result; useful singular-value/gradient distinction.

title: Gating creates slow modes and controls phase-space complexity in GRUs and LSTMs
venue: Mathematical and Scientific Machine Learning, PMLR 107:476–511
notes: Random GRU/LSTM mean-field and Jacobian analyses distinguish long-lived slow modes and gate-controlled stability/complexity. Useful recurrent/spiking-controller baselines but not a claim about subjective internal state.

title: Transition to chaos separates learning regimes and relates to measure of consciousness in recurrent neural networks
notes: Compares transition-to-chaos, trained representation behavior, and perturbational complexity proxies in specific RNN experiments. CRITICAL boundary: neural-dynamics correlation and PCIst proxy are not proof of subjective experience, artificial feelings or machine consciousness.

title: What Makes Recurrence Effective in Looped Language Models?
notes: Separates beyond-train-horizon reasoning improvements from knowledge degradation; more difficult items do not monotonically benefit from extra loops. Studies output/prelude placement, history-state injection, channel conditioning. Source-attributed preprint results, not accepted cross-model guarantee.

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
notes: Tests reachability, input dependence and local geometry of fixed points; recall placement and outer normalization on small chess/sudoku/prefix-sum experiments. Formal hypotheses have architecture-specific assumptions; not a general guarantee of LLM reasoning.

title: SCORE: Replacing Layer Stacking with Contractive Recurrent Depth
notes: ODE-inspired discrete shared-block step-size update across GNN/MLP/nanoGPT; source reports convergence/training gains. Contractive *parameterization* is not a validated task-sufficiency/efficient-scheduling result.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
notes: Attributes loop-training instability to residual explosion/gradient oscillation; compares fully looped routing and attention-injection changes, source-reported stabilization up to 12 loops. Separate training effects from inference-only depth tuning.

title: CART: Context-Anchored Recurrent Transformer -- A Parameter-Efficient Architecture with Learned Stability
notes: Important negative control: learned stable LTI gate (reported spectral radius .79–.83) yet lower performance than dense parameter-parity model and degradation when unrolling below/above trained R. Public code, training scripts and results database linked from arXiv; no general proof recurrence fails.

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
notes: Strong compositional synthetic task baseline with graph reachability, nested logic and relational text; preprint claims depth recurrence extrapolates on graph masking and uses final-only supervision, LayerScale, identity-biased gating. Revised v2 title/claims pinned; structured synthetic tasks are not general-world factual LMs.

title: Stabilizing Equilibrium Models by Jacobian Regularization
notes: Train-time Jacobian regularization for DEQ fixed-point convergence, including WikiText-103 and ImageNet in evaluated recipes. Public code https://github.com/locuslab/deq. This is not a full-spectrum Lyapunov estimator, nor a free inference-time stability change.

title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited
notes: Centered kernel alignment vs CCA for comparing networks trained from different initializations, with proof of high-dimensional invertible-invariant similarity limitations. Descriptive geometric agreement != functional transfer/causal sufficiency.

title: Optimal short-term memory before the edge of chaos in driven random recurrent networks
notes: Mean-field driven random RNN predicts short-term memory peak before autonomous edge of chaos in studied small-input regime. A controlled counterexample to naive 'maximum chaos => maximum memory' inference, not a general LLM or mobile-device performance rule.

title: Non-normal Recurrent Neural Network (nnRNN): learning long time dependencies while improving expressivity with transient dynamics
notes: Uses Schur normal/non-normal decomposition to allow stable spectra with transient amplification and sequence expressivity; exemplifies why eigenvalue stability and finite-horizon singular gain require separate measures.

title: Coding with transient trajectories in recurrent neural networks
notes: Stable non-normal recurrent linear systems can selectively amplify stimulus-aligned transients; analytic condition based on symmetric part and low-rank prescribed trajectories. Controlled task/output positive reference, not demonstration in trained Transformers.

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
notes: RLTT distributes training reward across latent recurrent trajectory; author-reported mathematics benchmark gains vs GRPO at Ouro 1.4B/2.6B, code https://github.com/jonwill8/RLTT. Training-heavy conditional follow-up, not a cheap offline finite-horizon diagnostic; process reward is not proof of readable hidden thoughts.

title: At the Edge of Chaos: Real-time Computations and Self-Organized Criticality in Recurrent Neural Networks
venue: NeurIPS 2004, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 17
notes: Early input-driven random threshold-network time-series memory/parity study reports high computational capability near criticality in that model family. Contrast with Haruna/Nakajima 2019 earlier-than-edge optimum: task, input and architecture conditional, not universal.

title: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity
notes: Date identifies the reviewed v3, not the original manuscript. Synthetic neural dynamics, observation models, and evaluation methods; source code inspected but not executed. Software release v1.0.2 and archived software DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22238472 are separate from this paper identity. No independent replication or project adoption asserted. Review depth: Primary indexed manuscript excerpts; author release citation and selected implementation inspected; full manuscript access limited.

title: Aligned and oblique dynamics in recurrent neural networks
notes: Reviewed v3 dated 2024-08-02. Separates output alignment with dominant activity from task information in low-variance directions and studies perturbation recovery. This is a controlled recurrent-network precedent, not a claim that arbitrary language-model compression is task sufficient. Review depth: Primary full HTML methods, perturbation results, and limitations inspected.

title: Beyond Geometry: Comparing the Temporal Structure of Computation in Neural Circuits with Dynamical Similarity Analysis
notes: DSA compares fitted temporal operators. A finite-data empirical similarity score does not independently certify topological conjugacy or identical algorithms; see the separately recorded Beyond DSA critique. Adequate trajectories and system-identification assumptions are required. Review depth: Primary paper/method illustration and author repository inspected.

title: InputDSA: Demixing then comparing recurrent and externally driven dynamics
notes: Separates intrinsic recurrence from external input drive in dynamical comparison. Full theorem/method package not independently audited. Short recurrent traces or absent input observations may not support the identification problem. No new accepted claim or general equivalence guarantee. Review depth: Primary metadata/abstract and implementation description; full methods review incomplete.

title: A metric for comparing complex systems by their dynamics
notes: Date refers to the reviewed v2. Dynamical-system comparison method; primary source identity and selected scope resolved, not an independently checked equivalence theorem or a replicated result. PubMed identity 42539270 provides a corroborating publication pointer. Review depth: Primary indexed manuscript and PubMed metadata; author implementation description.

title: Fast dynamical similarity analysis
notes: Reviewed revision dated 2026-04-01. Faster dynamical-comparison method; performance and validity remain tied to its identified operator/data assumptions. No execution or transfer to short-horizon language-model traces is claimed. Review depth: Primary metadata/abstract and implementation pointer.

title: Comparing noisy neural population dynamics using optimal transport distances
notes: Noise-aware temporal comparison using optimal transport; a comparator for observation/noise controls rather than evidence that geometrically similar trajectories implement the same computation. No independent reproduction performed. Review depth: Primary metadata and abstract.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
notes: Direct predecessor for initialization/path independence and useful test-time computation. Independence from initialization for a fixed input must not be confused with ignoring the input. Model-, task-, and intervention-specific results are not universal recurrent reasoning guarantees. Review depth: Primary NeurIPS paper, methods, and figure inspected.

title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
notes: Separates training-time trajectory effects from inference-time halting/readout selection. Compare stopping policies on identical frozen trajectories; an improvement after retraining does not identify which component caused the gain. No independent experimental replication. Review depth: Primary PDF methods and evaluation figure inspected in preceding audit; metadata reconfirmed.

title: Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models
notes: Separates common score motion from answer-changing motion. Retrospective completed-trajectory opportunities and prefix-only prediction are different outcomes; the proposed geometric predictor must face mean-centered and richer trained comparators. Answer preservation is not correctness. Review depth: Primary full HTML, predictive comparisons and discussion; canonical metadata checked.

title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
notes: Reviewed v2 dated 2026-09-25. Existing depth-aware batching, boundary-stage scheduling, and cache-policy baseline. H100/controlled-replay results do not certify small-device batch-one energy or latency; fewer loops need not yield proportional runtime savings. Review depth: Primary full HTML including scheduling, replay/hardware setup and cache discussion.

title: The Curious Case of In-Training Compression of State Space Models
notes: CompreSSM; reviewed revision 2026-02-24. Controllability/observability and Hankel-inspired state reduction during training. Linear-system guarantees do not automatically transfer to selective/nonlinear models. Projection diagnostics alone do not establish a smaller executable model. Review depth: Primary full HTML and selective-model limitations.

title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint v1 and author technical report
notes: Jacobian lens; author report https://www.transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html. ArXiv date/authors recorded here; report release is a separate surface. Sparse local J-space construction is not one universal low-rank linear plane. Functional workspace observations do not establish subjective experience; code is unmaintained reference code. Review depth: Author technical report and reference implementation; canonical arXiv metadata checked.

title: Functional Alignment Can Mislead: Examining Model Stitching
notes: Adversarial comparator for claims from successful model stitching. A useful stitched predictor does not by itself prove native representational equivalence or identical algorithms. Keep task utility, adapter capacity, and mechanistic explanation separate. Review depth: Primary proceedings metadata and abstract.

title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
notes: Metadata follows the four-author published proceedings; the earlier three-author arXiv record is a versioned variant, not a different paper. Behavior-changing interventions can exploit dormant pathways. Retain the methodological reply and success controls; not a claim that all activation patching is invalid. Review depth: Primary ICLR proceedings identity and abstract; author code pointer.

title: A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s "Interpretability Illusion" Arguments
notes: Methodological reply on subspace intervention interpretation. Keep both sides of the patching dispute and test control design rather than treating either position as a universal theorem. No independent replication or adjudication recorded. Review depth: Primary metadata and abstract.

title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM
notes: Message-content and intervention controls challenge interpreting aggregate gains as communication. Receiver-solvability, sender-specific necessary information, shuffled/irrelevant messages and matched-capacity controls are distinct tests. No universal rejection of latent communication or equivalence from nonsignificance. Review depth: Primary full HTML in preceding audit; indexed abstract identity checked.

title: Information Processing Capacity of Dynamical Systems
notes: Input-history function reconstruction separates memory and nonlinear processing under explicit input/readout assumptions. Capacity is not subjective experience, nor does optimizing a Lyapunov exponent alone establish useful task computation. Review depth: Primary full article.

title: Cortical Areas Interact through a Communication Subspace
notes: Online publication date recorded; issue publication 2019-04-03. Biological cross-area predictive subspaces are a methodological analogy, not a learned translator between arbitrary language-model states or proof of causal semantic transfer. Review depth: Primary publisher/PMC abstract and metadata.

title: Cortical activity in the null space: permitting preparation without movement
notes: Immediate output-null activity may remain relevant to later computation. Biological result supplies a horizon-relative measurement caution, not proof of a language-model mechanism. Review depth: Primary publisher/author abstract and metadata.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
notes: Foundational learned adaptive-computation/halting precedent. Additional computation and its stopping rule are established research topics; the original method is not automatically a drop-in policy for a different recurrent model or runtime. Review depth: Primary arXiv identity and abstract.

title: Universal Transformers
notes: Shared recurrent depth and adaptive computation in Transformers. Recurrence alone is not a new architecture claim; comparisons must account for training, task, capacity, and executed compute. Review depth: Primary arXiv identity/abstract and author explanation.

title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
notes: Probabilistic learned halting baseline. Training the trajectory and choosing an inference readout are separate interventions. No general inference-cost or correctness guarantee is imported. Review depth: Primary arXiv identity and abstract.

title: Analyzing Populations of Neural Networks via Dynamical Model Embedding
notes: DYNAMO learns representations of network populations from dynamics/outputs. It is a method comparator with its own fitting costs and assumptions, not proof that latent geometry identifies a unique algorithm. Review depth: Primary canonical metadata and abstract.

title: Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control
venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 15(1), 142–161
notes: DMDc separates intrinsic dynamics and measured actuation/input in a fitted operator model. Input observability, sufficient excitation, data length, and approximation limits matter; do not identify a high-dimensional system from a handful of recurrent states by assumption. Review depth: Primary publisher abstract and method scope.

title: Characterizing Dynamics with Covariant Lyapunov Vectors
notes: Covariant direction estimation is distinct from QR orthonormal frames and finite-horizon singular vectors. Identifying a functional role for a direction requires an additional task-sensitive test; no new algorithmic result is adopted. Review depth: Primary publisher/author abstract and metadata.

title: Dynamical Entropy Production in Spiking Neuron Networks in the Balanced State
notes: Existing full-spectrum calculation for a specific balanced spiking-network model. Event-driven dynamics, finite perturbations, and smooth surrogate training gradients must be distinguished; no controller efficiency or consciousness claim follows. Review depth: Primary publisher/arXiv abstract.

title: Saltation Matrices: The Essential Tool for Linearizing Hybrid Dynamical Systems
notes: Reference for event-time and reset-map variational derivatives. Smooth autodiff or surrogate spike gradients do not automatically equal the actual hybrid trajectory derivative; grazing/simultaneous-event assumptions require attention. Review depth: Primary publisher/arXiv abstract and metadata.

title: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling
notes: CALM: local early-exit confidence with sequence-level calibration and missing-state handling. Its population/risk guarantee depends on the declared calibration assumptions and does not imply per-answer correctness or arbitrary distribution-shift robustness. Independent-layer exits are not automatically recurrent-loop implementations. Review depth: Primary arXiv metadata and full HTML method/calibration discussion.

title: FREE: Fast and Robust Early-Exiting Framework for Autoregressive Language Models with Synchronized Parallel Decoding
notes: Existing synchronized-decoding and early-exit comparator. Fewer layers, hidden-state copying, and actual latency are different outcomes; copying hidden states versus projected KV caches changes semantics and must be tested. Review depth: Primary ACL proceedings metadata, abstract and method scope.

title: Fast yet Safe: Early-Exiting with Risk Control
notes: Risk-calibrated early exits; reviewed v2 dated 2024-11-04. IID calibration/test sampling and method-specific marginal-monotonicity assumptions must be checked. Learn-then-test and monotone-risk procedures differ. Average exits/FLOPs are not measured deployment energy, and relative agreement is not absolute correctness. Review depth: Primary arXiv metadata and full HTML risk assumptions/methods.

title: Grounding Representation Similarity Through Statistical Testing
notes: Published title uses Through; the arXiv title variant uses with. Same work, not duplicate identities. Evaluates whether representation metrics detect functional changes and tolerate irrelevant transformations; no descriptive metric by itself certifies causal task-state equivalence. Review depth: Primary NeurIPS proceedings abstract and bibliographic metadata.

title: Beyond DSA: Conjugacy-based Comparison of Dynamical Systems
notes: Authors' indexed abstract reports orthogonal Koopman alignment is neither necessary nor sufficient for topological conjugacy and proposes candidate-bijection alignment. Identity and abstract scope resolved; full proof and version-specific methods remain unreviewed. No theorem is imported as accepted evidence. Review depth: Primary indexed arXiv abstract and identity only; direct full-text retrieval unavailable.

title: Empirical Minimal-Realisation Compression of Deep Neural Networks via Controllability-Observability Tests
notes: Authors describe empirical reachability/observability reduction and actual reduced networks on MNIST/CIFAR-10. Primary abstract only; reported accuracy/compression/latency not independently verified. Distinguish an executable reduced network from projecting diagnostics while retaining the full model. Review depth: Primary indexed arXiv abstract and identity only; direct full-text retrieval unavailable.

title: A Negative Result on Cross-Model Activation Transfer in a Pythia Multi-Hop Setting
notes: Identity follows the initial primary indexed author/abstract record. A later two-author v2 lead was found but not independently resolved from a primary full page; no claim of current complete authorship. Source-reported failure of a post-hoc linear activation bridge does not reject all learned C2C communication. Review depth: Primary indexed arXiv initial abstract; later revision metadata and full methods unresolved.

title: Partial observation can induce mechanistic mismatches in data-constrained models of neural dynamics
notes: Authors show partial observations can produce surrogate models with spurious attractor structure despite matching observed single-unit dynamics. Primary abstract reviewed; large full PDF was not read in this pass. Good activity fit does not establish a faithful latent mechanism. Review depth: Primary NeurIPS proceedings metadata/abstract; full PDF fetch exceeded size limit.

title: Characterizing control between interacting subsystems with deep Jacobian estimation
notes: JacobianODE estimates nonlinear interactions/control between subsystems in its learned dynamical-model setting. When an exact frozen model is available, native autodiff/perturbation checks are preferable to an unnecessary surrogate. Not proof of arbitrary pretrained cross-model state translation. Review depth: Primary NeurIPS/arXiv metadata and abstract.

title: Expressive dynamics models with nonlinear injective readouts enable reliable recovery of latent features from neural activity
venue: Proceedings on Learning, Control and Dynamical Systems, PMLR 228:255–278
notes: ODIN; proceedings published in 2024 for a December 2023 event. Nonlinear injective readout is a controlled latent-recovery comparator. Readout capacity, observation fit, and correct latent dynamics are separate quantities; no general identifiability theorem for language-model states is claimed. Review depth: Primary PMLR proceedings metadata and abstract; selected method context.

title: On the difficulty of learning chaotic dynamics with RNNs
notes: Relates training-gradient behavior and Lyapunov dynamics when learning chaotic systems. Forcing stability can destroy desired chaotic target behavior. Reconstruction of chaotic data is not evidence that chaos improves language-model reasoning or that every gradient instability is a numerical bug. Review depth: Primary NeurIPS/arXiv abstract and canonical metadata.
